newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria buys 100,000 tonnes of wheat at $183-184.
newsitem.headline: Algeria buys 100,000 tonnes of wheat at $183-184.

text.p: Algeria on Thursday bought 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat from two trade houses at between $183 and $184 per tonne including freight, European grain traders said.
The four wheat cargoes, for May/June shipment, could come at least partly from France despite the reported exclusion of French firms from recent Algerian purchase tenders, they said.
Exporters have said French firms were isolated from Algerian grain purchases last month after a French leader's remarks on democracy provoked an angry public response from Algiers.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe called on television in March for a "true democratic conscience" to be established in Algeria.
The absence of French operators did not however exclude foreign intermediaries from selling French wheat, traders said.
The two companies said to have sold wheat on Thursday do not have their headquarters in France.
Algeria launched a snap tender on Tuesday for four 25,000 tonne cargoes of wheat for late May and early June shipment.
Although operators initially said the tender was for North American wheat only, an Algerian official afterwards denied this and declared the tender open to all suppliers of the grain.
